title: Dryer Vent Cleaning: How Often for Condos vs. Houses?
h1: How Often Should a Dryer Vent Be Cleaned in a Condo vs. a House?
description: Most dryer vents should be cleaned about once a year, and condos with long or roof vents often need it sooner. Here's how to set the right schedule.
quick_answer: Plan on cleaning most dryer vents about once a year. Condos and townhomes often need it more often, because their vents tend to run long distances through walls and ceilings or exit through the roof. Single-family homes with short, straight vents to an outside wall can sometimes go a little longer. Slow drying or weak airflow means it's due now.
body:
A yearly cleaning is a good baseline for most homes. From there, adjust based on how your vent is built and how much laundry you do. A short, straight vent through an outside wall stays cleaner. A long run through the ceiling to the roof, which is common in condos, collects lint much faster.

Why do condos usually need more frequent cleaning?

Condo and townhome laundry closets are often in the middle of the unit, far from an outside wall. To get air outside, the vent has to travel up and across, sometimes through other floors, before it exits through the roof. That creates a few problems:

  • Longer runs. More duct means more surface for lint to stick to.
  • More turns. Every elbow slows airflow and catches lint.
  • Vertical rises. Lint has to be pushed uphill, and some falls back down.
  • Roof exits. Roof caps clog with lint and sometimes bird nests, and they're hard to check yourself.
  • Limited access. Parts of the run may be hidden behind drywall.

Because of this, many condo vents benefit from cleaning every six months to a year, especially in a busy household.

How often should a vent be cleaned in a single-family house?

Many San Diego and Orange County houses have the laundry in the garage or along an exterior wall, with a short vent straight outside. Those setups clog slowly, and a yearly check is often plenty. Some go a bit longer if laundry loads are light.

Houses aren't always simple, though. Second-floor laundry rooms, vents that run through the attic and vents that exit the roof behave more like condo setups. Attic runs can sag between supports, and the low spots hold lint and moisture.

What changes the schedule?

Clean more often if any of these apply:

  • A large family or daily laundry loads
  • Pets that shed a lot
  • Lots of towels, blankets or fleece, which shed heavy lint
  • Foil or plastic flex hose anywhere in the run
  • A vent near the manufacturer's maximum length
  • Vents that run through a hot attic or sag between supports

What signs mean the vent needs cleaning now?

Don't wait for the calendar if you notice:

  • Clothes needing more than one cycle to dry
  • The dryer or laundry room getting unusually hot
  • A burning or scorched smell
  • Weak airflow at the outside vent or a flap that barely opens
  • Lint around the outside hood or behind the dryer
  • A dryer that shuts off before the cycle ends

Some newer dryers show a vent warning light. Take it seriously, since it means the dryer is sensing restricted airflow.

Who is responsible for cleaning a condo dryer vent?

It depends on your HOA. In some buildings, the association handles roof caps and shared portions, while owners are responsible for the run from their dryer to the wall. In others, the owner handles everything. Check your HOA rules before scheduling, and ask whether roof access needs to be arranged.

Our dryer vent cleaning crews clean condo and house vents across San Diego County and Orange County, including roof exits. We'll clear the full run, check the cap or hood and tell you if anything is crushed, disconnected or too long.

Why does dryer vent cleaning matter so much?

Lint is highly flammable, and a dryer vent puts it right next to a heat source. As lint builds up, airflow drops, the dryer runs hotter and longer, and the heating element or burner cycles more. That combination is how dryer fires start.

A clear vent also saves wear on the dryer itself. Restricted airflow makes the motor, thermostats and heating parts work harder, and clothes take longer to dry, which adds up over a year of laundry.

What can you do between cleanings?

Clean the lint screen every load and wash it occasionally. Keep the dryer a few inches from the wall so the hose doesn't crush. Use a metal transition hose. And if you can see the outside hood, check it every few months for lint and nests.
faqs: How often should a condo dryer vent be cleaned?

Many condo vents need cleaning every six months to a year because they run long distances and often exit through the roof. Busy households and vents with several turns sit at the shorter end of that range.
Can I clean my dryer vent myself?

You can clean the lint screen, the transition hose and a short, straight vent with a brush kit. Long runs, roof exits and vents hidden in walls are better left to a professional with the right tools and safe roof access.
Does my HOA clean my dryer vent?
Some do and some don't. Many HOAs cover roof caps or shared ducts, while owners handle the part inside their unit. Check your association's rules before scheduling.
